text: A VPC is an isolated, private network you define inside an AWS Region — your own address space, carved out with a CIDR block like 10.0.0.0/16.
A subnet is a slice of that address range, confined to exactly one Availability Zone. Public subnets have a route to the internet, private subnets don't.
What makes a subnet public isn't a label on it — it's its route table. An Internet Gateway attaches to the VPC, and a public subnet's route table sends internet-bound traffic there.
Security groups are stateful and attach to resources; network ACLs are stateless and apply at the subnet level. Next up: AWS pricing and cost management.
